newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Flooding hits over 2,000 homes in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Flooding hits over 2,000 homes in Romania.

text.p: Landslides and flooding caused by heavy rains over the weekend damaged more than 2,000 homes in the foothills south of the Carpathian mountains in Romania, but no new casualties were reported, officials said on Monday.

"The situation in Prahova county is extremely difficult due more to landslides than to flooding caused by the rain at the weekend," Viorel Raicu, State secretary at the Environment Ministry, said by telephone.
The landslides damaged more than 2,000 homes in towns and villages in Prahova and Dimbovita counties north of Bucharest, the Environment Ministry said.
The authorities despatched trucks with drinking water to the worst hit area of Breaza, 160 km (100 miles) north of Bucharest, where the landslides had damaged 1,800 houses.

The floods have claimed six lives in Romania over the last two weeks where the impact of the heavy rains have been less dramatic than in Poland, Germany, and the Czech Republic, but more rain is expected across the country this week.
Thousands of hectares of Romanian cropland have been submerged in western and southeast regions, although grain producing areas in central and southern Romania have been spared the worst.

Floodwaters had receded by Monday and workers had started to repair damaged roads and restore water and power supplies, but the total cost and extent of the damage caused by the rains is not yet known.
Raicu said flood monitors were keeping a close eye on the Romanian section of the River Danube whose water level had been higher than normal but below flood stage over the past few days.
"The dikes in the area where the River Danube bends northwards, towards the (river) port of Braila, have been reinforced, but so far there is no reason for alarm," he said.
